messages:
anya: heads up — saw a regression on the canary after the kernel-selection change. when running long-context streaming workloads (+~50k tokens) with continuous batching we get steady memory growth and periodic head-of-line stalls.
anya: reproduced locally with loadgen: 12 clients, 4k qps, ctx=60k, cont-batching=on. heap grows ~600MB/hr until OOM if left long enough.
sasha: yikes. any flamegraph or heapshot? reproducible with a single model?
anya: yep repro with gpt-ish-8b quant model. attaching a tiny profiler snippet below (pasted):
```
perf top snapshot:
  kvcache::page_pin             32.4%  <-- hot
  kvcache::merge_batches        18.7%
  kvcache::evict_try           12.1%
  runtime::kernel_dispatch     10.3%
  alloc::large_page_mmap        8.5%
```
anya: also saw many small page allocations in the allocator logs and kv-slot refcounts never drop to zero for some pages.
bench-bot: benchmark summary (canary run 2024-08-14):
- sustained latency p95 up ~30ms
- memory delta +590MB after 2h
- HOL stalls observed during batch-merge events
deploy-bot: deploy log: kernel-selection patch rolled to canary at 10:21 UTC, rollback at 15:03 after OOM alerts.
prashant: my take — kernel change altered eviction tempo. continuous-batching merges batches across clients which sometimes pins pages while merge completes; if merge repeatedly splits/joins the same fragment we get fragmentation + refcount churn so eviction can't compact. head-of-line happens when a large batch owns early slots and other smaller batches block waiting for contiguous pages.
sasha: sounds plausible. any quick dumps we can look at? kv page map + batch ownership table?
anya: posted a kv dump excerpt:
```
# kv_page table (page_id, refcnt, owner_batch)
(0x1a3, 2, batch_122)
(0x1a4, 0, free)
(0x1a5, 3, batch_119)
(0x1a6, 1, merge_op:batch_119+batch_122)
... many small pages with refcnt 1 and owner=merge_op
```
prashant: those merge_op owners are the smoking gun — we create transient merge objects that hold refs while we stitch k/v fragments. if merge_op lifetime > eviction window pages will never be reclaimed, and repeated split/merge causes fragmentation.
miguel: two quick mitigations we can try: 1) short-term: add a cap so merge_op refs are ephemeral — move merging to an async task that yields regularly and relinquishes page refs between steps; 2) mid-term: make eviction batch-aware — allow evict to preempt merge_ops on a best-effort basis and insert a lightweight compaction pass.
sasha: can we just stop cross-client batch merging for ctx > 16k? that should avoid HOL for long contexts without big perf hit for short ctx.
anya: yes, toggled cont-batching.max_merge_context to 16k locally and the heap stopped growing in the 2h test. latency increased ~8ms p95 but no OOM.
prashant: good data. long-term we still want merging for efficiency on short contexts so need smarter ownership and defrag. propose: add per-page generation ID and allow atomic transfer of ownership during merge so eviction can see pending-transfer pages and compact them. also schedule periodic defrag when free pages > threshold.
miguel: agree. also think kernel-selection should expose a k/v eviction pressure metric so runtime can choose kernels that produce less fragmentation for long-context jobs.
anya: open to landing a hotfix: (A) clamp merge across clients when ctx > 16k, (B) make merge_op yield every 50ms and drop page refs between steps. I'll prototype (B).
sasha: please file an RFC-ish issue with repro steps + benchmarks.
prashant: I'll mock up the generation-ID sketch and a simple compactor. want to try on canary next week.
bench-bot: action items recorded: AN-1 clamp merge ctx (anya) AN-2 async-yield merge (anya) AN-3 gen-id + compactor (prashant) AN-4 add eviction-pressure metric (miguel).
deploy-bot: noted — schedule canary for AN-1 + AN-2 after unit tests.
anya: repro steps in brief: run loadgen scenario "long-stream-merge" (repo/tests/long_stream.py) with ctx=60k, cont-batching enabled, measure mem after 2h.
sasha: thanks — if you can attach the small heapshots and the perf top when you open the issue that helps.
miguel: ping me if you need a quick kernel revert for bisecting.
anya: thanks all, starting the async-yield prototype now. will update thread with microbench numbers. :thumbsup:
